newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU threatens Belgium over aerial photography curbs.
newsitem.headline: EU threatens Belgium over aerial photography curbs.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it could take legal action against Belgium unless it lifted curbs on foreign firms which wanted to take aerial pictures over the country.
"Companies from other (European Union) member states wishing to undertake aerial photography over Belgium are refused permission to do so," the Commission said in a statement.
The Commission considers the restrictions placed on aerial photography over Belgium violate EC Treaty rules on the freedom to provide services and the freedom of establishment.
Belgium insists that aerial photography can only be undertaken by companies based in the country using Belgian- registered aircraft.
"Following complaints from companies wishing to undertake aerial photography over Belgium, the Commission is pursuing infringement proceedures," the Commission statement said.
Belgium has 40 working days to respond, after which "The Commission could refer the case to the (European) Court of Justice." -- Paul de Bendern, Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 6812, Fax 32 2 230 7710
